prompt.context: Rock Energy, an Oil & Gas company, is evaluating the purchase of one of three oil fields in Latin America. After Rock Energy has decided which oil field to purchase, it will outsource all drilling related activities. You have been brought in to identify the best investment for Rock Energy.
prompt.question: How would you evaluate the three oil fields, and which oil field should Rock Energy purchase?

clarifying_info.q: How long do the drilling rights last, and when does production begin?
clarifying_info.a: The rights give Rock Energy the right to drill during year 1 and produce oil for 20 years. Assume no oil is produced until the beginning of year 2.

clarifying_info.q: How many rigs can operate in each region?
clarifying_info.a: Rock Energy can deploy a maximum of 10 rigs concurrently in each of the regions.

clarifying_info.q: What does the cost per rig day include?
clarifying_info.a: The cost per rig day includes crew, consumables, and services.
Any amount of oil extracted will be sold at the spot market price at the moment.

clarifying_info.q: Do the wells require maintenance costs over the 20-year production period?
clarifying_info.a: For simplicity, assume the oil wells will produce the same amount of oil for the next 20 years with no maintenance costs.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost to acquire the drilling rights?
clarifying_info.a: The rights to extract oil cost $40M in each region.

clarifying_info.q: What is the price of oil?
clarifying_info.a: The spot price of oil is $50 per barrel.

exhibits.title: Oil Field Profiles, 2010
exhibits.shows: A table and two bar charts comparing the three regions on drilling rate (meters/day), average depth of wells (meters), maximum concurrent rigs, average well production (barrels per day), and cost per rig day.

data.note: Wells are continuously dug during year 1 (assume 360 days). Oil is extracted beginning of year 2. Once a well is completed, the rig moves on to dig another well.

framework: Revenues: price of oil × barrels extracted per well × number of wells drilled in year 1, aggregated across all rigs per region
Costs: investment cost (rights to extract oil, $40M per region) + drilling costs (days to complete a well × cost per rig day × number of wells)
Profitability: Total Revenue − Total Cost for each region; also assess profit per well and profit margin per well
Operational factors: drilling speed (depth ÷ penetration rate), rig utilization, number of wells achievable per rig in 360 days
Qualitative / risk factors: insurance costs, political stability, labor contracts and unions, oil price volatility, oil quality differences across regions
Investment selection: compare total profit across regions to identify the best investment

questions.prompt: Calculate the time to complete one well in each region.
questions.guidance: Time to complete a well = Average depth ÷ Drilling rate (penetration rate). Candidate should use data from Exhibit 1.

math.answer: Region 1 = 60 days; Region 2 = 90 days; Region 3 = 180 days

questions.prompt: Calculate the number of wells that can be drilled per region in year 1 (360 days, 10 rigs).
questions.guidance: Wells per year = (360 ÷ days per well) × number of rigs. All regions have 10 rigs max.

math.setup: Wells per year = (360 ÷ time per well) × 10 rigs
math.answer: Region 1 = 60 wells; Region 2 = 40 wells; Region 3 = 20 wells

questions.prompt: Calculate the cost per well for each region.
questions.guidance: Cost per well = Days to complete well × Cost per rig day.

math.setup: Cost per well = time per well (days) × cost per rig day ($)

questions.prompt: Calculate the yearly revenue per well for each region (production begins year 2).
questions.guidance: Yearly revenue per well = Price per barrel × daily production × 360 days.

math.setup: Yearly revenue per well = $50/bbl × barrels/day × 360 days

questions.prompt: What are the first-year profits for each region (year 1 = drilling, year 2 = first production year)?
questions.guidance: Total Revenue = Yearly revenue per well × number of wells. Total Cost = (Cost per well × number of wells) + $40M rights. Profit = Total Revenue − Total Cost. Candidate should note that even though Region 1 has the highest per-well profit margin (500%), Region 2 wins on total profit because it drills 40 wells vs. 60 for Region 1 but earns far more per well. Region 3 yields a net loss.

math.setup: Profit per well = Yearly revenue per well − Cost per well. Total Revenue = Yearly revenue per well × wells. Total Cost = (Cost per well × wells) + $40,000,000. Profit = Total Revenue − Total Cost.

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors or risks should Rock Energy consider before finalizing its investment decision?

categories.name: Financial / Cost risks
ideas: Insurance costs for drilling operations and assets
Oil price volatility — spot price could fall significantly over the 20-year production horizon
Currency risk if costs or revenues are denominated in different currencies
Cost overruns in drilling if geological conditions differ from estimates

categories.name: Operational risks
ideas: Actual penetration rates may differ from averages shown in Exhibit 1
Equipment availability and rig supply constraints
Well completion risk — some wells may not produce as expected
Logistics and infrastructure access in each Latin American region

categories.name: Political / Regulatory risks
ideas: Political stability of the host country in each region
Changes in royalty, tax, or nationalization policies

categories.name: Market / Strategic risks
ideas: Oil quality differences across regions affecting realized price
Availability of qualified outsourced drilling operators
Opportunity cost — are there other investment alternatives?
Expected value analysis assigning different probabilities to the barrels-per-day estimates

recommendation: Rock Energy should invest in buying the rights for Region 2, which generates the highest total first-year profit of $68M.

Although Region 1 has a higher per-well profit margin (500% vs. 300%), Region 2's larger per-well output and revenue more than compensate, yielding $18M more total profit than Region 1 despite fewer wells drilled.
Region 3 should be rejected outright as it produces a net loss of $4M in the first production year.
risks: Oil price volatility over the 20-year production period could erode returns for all regions.
Political instability in the Latin American region where Region 2 is located could disrupt operations.
Actual well production rates may deviate from the 200 bbl/day average assumed, changing the ranking.
Labor or union issues with the outsourced drilling operator could increase costs or delay drilling.
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on the political and regulatory environment specific to Region 2's country.
Model sensitivity of total profit to oil price changes and production rate variance.
Perform an expected value analysis assigning probabilities to different barrels-per-day outcomes for each region.
Negotiate drilling contracts with outsourced operators to lock in cost per rig day before committing to the rights purchase.
